source: William Lilly Christian Astrology 1647 original Wellcome b30338724
source_study_note: This original chapter comprises aesthetic appearance, alleged temperament, dignity/wealth/dowry, position aphorisms, and married trouble; all historical social, gender, medical, sexual stereotypes and unverified source-only.

groups.source_group: Original CXXXIIII wife character, beauty and bodily classification source input

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Printed CXXXIIII is a distinct section on a presumed wife and her characteristics; it includes more than only appearance.
Seventh-house cusp sign is named as one source indicator for alleged spouse appearance.
The source also considers the planet especially signifying wife as a separate contributor.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planets beholding Moon she applying unto them
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Moon's applying aspect to other planets supplies further conditions in source, not just occupants of seventh.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: either by Conjunction or any other partill aspect
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Author specifies conjunction or another partile aspect, not any arbitrary distant aspect.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: all or most these in Signes of pulchritude
clauses.historical_source_meaning: The good-looking/ill-looking result is based on all or most indicators, not a single sign match.
The seventeenth-century social-aesthetic result is a historical stereotype and not an actual partner forecast.
The author assigns stigmatizing bodily labels from zodiac configurations, not an observed disability or diagnosis.

groups.source_group: Zodiac sign category lists and Saturn or solar combustion appearance exceptions

clauses.historical_source_meaning: The source lists Gemini, Virgo, Libra and a portion of Sagittarius among 'fair' examples, exact portion glyph checked against original separately.
Source has a separate intermediate beauty category, rather than only fair/deformed dichotomy.
The source provides a separate multi-sign negative category, with later Scorpio and Sagittarius portions glyph-sensitive.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: latter part of Scorpio and Sagittarius
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Subsign boundaries and several old astrological glyphs are not sufficiently certain to encode as runnable predicate.
Saturn is singled out for period appearance stereotyping.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn afflict Significators with evil aspect
clauses.historical_source_meaning: The Saturn negative branch requires aspects to the already selected spouse signifiers.
Sun combustion alleged to change spouse complexion, not medical knowledge.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus with Saturn in Terms of Saturn
clauses.historical_source_meaning: One claimed spouse-age case involves Venus linked to Saturn and in Saturn's bounds.
Saturn's aspect to Venus is an alternative for allegedly older spouse, not necessarily conjunction.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: old woman or more years than his age
clauses.historical_source_meaning: The claimed outcome is spouse older than native, a distinct objective target from appearance.
A separate classic source rule alleges older spouse from paired malefics in seventh.

groups.source_group: Benefic-looking spouse aspects, Jupiter caveats and widow/marital-history alternatives

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Jupiter, Venus and Moon favorable mutual configurations are described as positive appearance cases.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: aspecting cusp seventh or principal Significator
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Positive configurations can aspect seventh cusp or spouse signifier, not necessarily share one house.
Alleged favorable wife appearance, no independently observed spouse ratings.
Having Jupiter in the seventh alone is not guaranteed favorable in the text.
Jupiter-Moon conjunction under additional circumstances may yield an unfavorable appearance, a counterexample to simple Jupiter goodness.
Negative Jupiter-Moon source claim itself depends on lacking supporting evidence; do not pull it out alone.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: I have proved true many times
clauses.historical_source_meaning: The author offers personal retrospective success assertion without denominator, adverse cases or blind verification.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter in seventh not essentially strong
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Jupiter weak condition is a further qualifier in distinct widow source branch.
Wife's prior marital status is allegedly inferred from chart, and must be separated from attractiveness.

groups.source_group: Source section Conditions of Wife, Ptolemy and earlier authors attributed

clauses.historical_source_meaning: An internal subsection changes target from appearance to personality/disposition.
Source uses a selected spouse-descriptor planet rather than asserting all visible planets equal weight.
Lilly attributes temperament schemes to Ptolemy and named later transmitters without source originals collated here.
Source names a chain of authors who purportedly borrow Ptolemy, not independent evidence of human accuracy.
Saturn branch requires the Moon applying to Saturn, not any natal Saturn condition.
Favorable Saturn gives taciturn, grave, sparing and industrious spouse stereotypes.
Negative Saturn gives stubbornness, laziness, envy, suspicion stereotypes.
The source explicitly reverses interpretations according to Saturn's condition, not simply Saturn present.

groups.source_group: Jupiter and Mars supposed spouse character branches

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Author says well-placed Jupiter may denote gentle, honest, chastity-coded and housekeeping virtues.
The source says nominal virtues can be obscured or not shown when planet poorly placed.
The Mars source condition requires Moon applying to Mars.
Author claims hearty, strong-willed disposition under good Mars, with historical gender-role assertions.
Period gender hierarchy stereotype, not evidence of any woman's actual agency or conduct.
Poorly dignified Mars allegedly predicts quarrelsome, violent or proud spouse.
Additional negative Mars labels are rhetorical, not independently measured temperament scales.

groups.source_group: Venus and Mercury Moon applications and important target exclusion

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Venus condition is Moon applying to Venus rather than mere Venus sign placement.
Venus good dignity supposedly leads attractiveness and social kindness, a combined behavior/appearance source claim.
Same source reverses to arrogance, talkativeness and alleged dishonesty with weak Venus.
Mercury condition includes conjunction or application.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury strong in dignities or free misfortune
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Good Mercury linked to eloquence, discretion and household care.
Poor Mercury linked to deceit, gossip, lying and turbulence without real verification.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Moon no manner of signification in conditions
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Lilly states Sun/Moon do not directly signify wife's temperament in THIS subsection; not universally inert in marriage rules.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: forme and shape framed according nature Planets and Signes
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Appearance mechanism is cross-referred to earlier planetary/sign rules rather than newly defined precise measurements.

groups.source_group: Internal Venus placement aphorisms: power, financial motive, low-status and sexuality claims

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Separate aphorism subsection remains within same printed chapter.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus Orientall essential dignities Jupiter aspect
clauses.historical_source_meaning: A composite favorable Venus condition and Jupiter aspect alleges domestic authority of spouse.
Period gender hierarchy prediction framed as a spouse household power outcome, not validated.
Venus second house allegedly denotes marrying for spouse wealth.
Venus sixth allegorizes spouse being of lower social standing; not an objective caste fact.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus fourth Square or Opposition Moon Aquarius
clauses.historical_source_meaning: A complex sign/house/aspect rule alleges sexual conduct, not established behavior.
Another alternate sign claimed to affect sexual conduct, not relationship count.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus in seventh native long ere marry
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Source predicts late marriage from Venus seventh house without age cutoff.
A separate pejorative sexual-label assertion has no reliable observational evidence.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus in eleventh cohabit woman having Children
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Source alleges partner's preexisting children/cohabitation, distinct from legal marriage or fertility.
Traditional class/charisma spouse prediction.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter aspect Venus in tenth more noble
clauses.historical_source_meaning: A Jupiter modifier strengthens social rank wording.

groups.source_group: Venus/Saturn/Mercury/Mars historical stigma, alleged fertility and infidelity

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Author alleges older, poor or allegedly dishonest partner from Saturn+Venus condition.
Saturn dignity is an additional qualifier for the Venus-first case.
Saturn dignity via Venus rulership is a separate alternative.
Period source associates placement with alleged low spouse character under other Saturn/tenth qualifiers.
Saturn tenth is additional condition in composite Venus-Mercury prediction.
Mars aspect is a further speculative severity modifier for moral/poisoning labels, not reliable warning.
Source's false-conduct allegations are not actual crime, poisoning, magic or dangerous-person prediction.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon fourth Venus with Saturn in tenth
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Historically asserts infertility or no children under combined factors; not a medical diagnosis.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: either age or defect of nature
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Two alternative alleged infertility explanations expand outcomes and must not be treated as one validated prediction.
A distinct source condition makes infidelity accusations; not evidence of real extramarital conduct.
Author claims inability to beget children, which is not actual fertility evidence.
Combined planetary company allegedly yields hard-working, caring wife and family relationship.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars with Venus full of spirit
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Another gender and sexual-morality label under planet combination, not observed private conduct.

groups.source_group: Final aphorism on planet associations and start of wife's riches

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Saturn-Venus unfavorable aspect alleged to intensify misconduct, an old moral stereotype.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter with Venus fairness cleanliness modesty
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Jupiter is associated with positive period-personal virtues, not real measured characteristics.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury varies for good or ill
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Author explicitly says Mercury changes interpretation by dignity, preventing one fixed Mercury result.
A new internal subsection about dowry, property and class rather than appearance.
The author evaluates planets aspecting Moon positively as input for wife wealth/social rank.
Conjunction is given as another input path for alleged spouse wealth.
Both benefic nature and dignity are required for the strongest wife wealth/rank source branch.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: rich and wealthy Wife well descended
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Alleged economic background claim, not independently confirmed asset records.

groups.source_group: Important social-class relativity proviso and beggar chart example

clauses.historical_source_meaning: The author reverses wife-wealth predictions for poorly dignified malefics.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: consider quality and birth of Native
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Lilly explicitly forbids assessing spouse's class without considering native's own class/background.
A strong benefic does NOT permit literal high-aristocratic title prediction irrespective of natal social group.
Author gives hypothetical beggar chart as example of beneficial marriage without literal nobility.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: daughter of some Tradesman or Farmer
clauses.historical_source_meaning: For beggar, spouse of tradesman/farmer family counts as well descended relatively.
Benefic allegedly indicates some dowry or support relative to current hardship, not guaranteed wealth absolute.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Marriage reduce poor man to better subsistence
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Author predicts relative improvement after marriage, no measured income baseline.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: not predict impossibilities but to every one Quod Capax
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Lilly states a source-level outcome ceiling relative to recipient social opportunity, weakening naive absolute forecasts.

groups.source_group: Seventh house benefics/malefics, ruler exchanges and spouse condition

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Fortunes either of them in seventh
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Benefic presence in seventh is another alleged wealth/dowry source.
Strength in seventh increases asserted wealth and quality.
Malefic presence indicates trouble but not always poverty.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if they be potent perhaps Wife may be rich
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Lilly explicitly says strong malefics may still indicate a wealthy spouse, contrary to simple bad=poor.
The author splits supposed wealth from spouse temperament even under same configuration.
One rulership exchange for a 'good wife' outcome.
The reciprocal exchange forms a distinct source alternative.
Author adds reciprocal second/seventh exchange as favorable spouse wealth/quality marker.
Second reciprocal alternative, not required with second-lord in seventh.

groups.source_group: Lower status branch and internal signs of a good Wife

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Source alleges a poor spouse/low birth under one ruler placement.
Reciprocal alternative for source class claim.
Subsection signals new outcome on quality/wealth/household rather than beauty.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: happy aspect Jupiter to Venus or Moon
clauses.historical_source_meaning: A beneficial aspect in an alleged good-wife source case.
Reception/essential dignity is an additional precondition for high status/riches.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: wealthy wife marriage with great Birth
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Period rank and class result not supported by objective registry.
Source associates house ruler in own house with honest/simple spouse.
Benefic-type seventh ruler in eighth is prerequisite for alleged inheritance source.
Claim of future inherited assets distinct from spouse current rank.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Kingly fixed Star first magnitude cusp seventh
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Rare first-magnitude star near seventh cusp is alleged to aid spouse wealth if cusp fortunate.
Star alone not sufficient; beneficial cusp condition is added.

groups.source_group: Internal Signs of ill fortune by Wife and genuine contradictory cases

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Signes of ill fortune by a Wife
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Another internal subsection addresses trouble attributed to marriage, not appearance.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Malignant Planets seventh very strong denote Riches
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Strong malefics can signal spouse wealth even in negative section, contrary to absolute no-wealth assumption.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: not attainable without scandall or trouble
clauses.historical_source_meaning: The good monetary source result is conditional on alleged scandal/trouble, a separate outcome.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Infortunes very imbecill seventh poor abject Wife
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Weak malefics are interpreted as poverty and class, without independent real couples.
One source negative branch places seventh ruler in sixth or twelfth.
Reverse source branch is an alternative, not an additional requirement.
Old hierarchical social characterization, not physical/medical/ethical classification.
Source severe-marriage branch with Saturn/Mars seventh, not necessarily both.
Benefic aspects are an explicit source exemption from the severe-malefic prediction.
The malefic severe branch also checks accidental house position, preventing simplistic seventh-only scoring.
The author ascribes difficulties to Saturn, a hypothesis lacking observed marriage outcomes.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars death and destruction before Native
clauses.historical_source_meaning: High-stakes mortality outcome is completely unsupported; not evidence a spouse will die.
An alleged conflict indicator distinct from death and financial claims.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus second in evil aspect malefics
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Another wealth/financial-harm source branch linked to Venus in second and adverse aspects.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon Lady seventh and posited eighth
clauses.historical_source_meaning: A specific lunar rulership and eighth-house prerequisite for decreased marriage joy.
Waning Moon is an additional source-specific modifier, not lunar position alone.
The result is an imprecise subjective satisfaction judgment, requiring externally defined scale before testing.

clauses.historical_source_meaning: Printed CXXXV starts after horizontal divider PDF631/printed597; separate pair dynamics chapter.

clauses.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Consider Planets shewing number of Wives
clauses.historical_source_meaning: Only first incipit of next chapter retained to verify boundary, not imported into preceding CXXXIIII.
